pictures.name: header
pictures.alt: Illustration of a row of objects on a shelf, from left to right: a round pebble, a walnut, a clay marble, a china marble, a handmade onionskin, a machine-made corkscrew and a cat's eye.
pictures.caption: From pebbles and nuts to glass. Illustration, not photos of historical objects.

pictures.name: timeline
pictures.alt: Illustrated timeline of marbles: stone balls at Mohenjo-daro around 2500 BCE; Roman children's nut games; Bruegel's 1560 painting of children at marbles; marble scissors in Lauscha around 1846; clay marbles mass-made in the US from the 1870s; Christensen's machine patent, filed 1902 and published 1905; tournaments from the 1920s and 1930s; cat's eyes common by the 1950s.
pictures.caption: Some milestones from this history, as an illustrated timeline. Illustration.

pictures.name: before-glass
pictures.alt: Illustration of what the earliest marbles may have been: round pebbles, nuts and fruit pits, and small stone balls, on bare earth.
pictures.caption: Before glass: pebbles, nuts and fruit pits, and small stone balls whose use is uncertain. An illustration, not a picture of particular finds.

pictures.name: marble-scissors
pictures.alt: Illustration of a glowing glass cane with a hot, newly rounded swirl marble at its end, held between the blades of a pair of marble scissors.
pictures.caption: Marble scissors cutting a marble from a glass cane, the method used in Lauscha from around 1846. Illustration.

pictures.name: christensen-machine
pictures.alt: Diagram of the principle of Christensen's marble machine: two grooved rolls turning in opposite directions roll a lump of soft glass into a ball between them, with a spring letting one roll move aside.
pictures.caption: The idea behind Christensen's machine (patent filed 1902, published 1905): two grooved rolls turning in opposite directions. A simplified illustration, not a copy of the patent drawing.
